title: The image of a closed immersion on an affine open is the zero locus of its ideal
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\to X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and $U\subseteq X$ an affine open with $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$; for $x\in U$ let $\mathfrak p_x\subset R$ be the prime ideal of $x$ under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $i(Z)$ is a closed subset of $X$ and $i(Z)\cap U=\{x\in U:\ \mathcal I(U)\subseteq\mathfrak p_x\}$, i.e. under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ the set $i(Z)\cap U$ corresponds to $V(\mathcal I(U))=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R:\mathcal I(U)\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IN (schemes-lemma-closed-subspace-scheme), parts (3) and (4): i^{-1}(U) -> U is identified with Spec(R/I) -> Spec(R) and I|_U = I~, so I = I(U); with Algebra, Lemma 00E5 (algebra-lemma-spec-closed, literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex): Spec(R/I) -> Spec(R) is a homeomorphism onto V(I)
